title: The Promise
subtitle: God Keeps His Word

pages.heading: A Big Boat
pages.text: Long ago the world had grown sad and full of wrong. But there was a man named Noah who loved God. God told Noah, “Build a great big boat.” So Noah did — hammer, hammer, hammer — even when it seemed strange. Then, two by two, the animals came: stomping elephants, hopping rabbits, flapping birds. Noah's family and all the animals climbed safely inside.

pages.heading: Waiting for Dry Land
pages.text: Then the rain came down, and the water rose high, but the big boat floated safely on top. For a long time they waited. One day Noah sent out a little dove to look for land. It came back carrying a fresh green leaf — a sign that somewhere, trees were growing again! Soon the ground was dry, and everyone stepped out into a fresh, clean world.

pages.heading: The Rainbow
pages.text: Then God painted something beautiful across the sky — a shining rainbow, curving from one side all the way to the other. It was a promise. “I will always take care of my world,” God said. And every time a rainbow appears, it whispers the same happy truth: God keeps every promise he ever makes.

verse.text: I have put my rainbow in the clouds. It will be the sign of my promise to the earth.

christ_connection.heading: The Promise Keeper
christ_connection.text: God always keeps his promises — the rainbow says so. And God made the biggest promise of all: that he would send a Rescuer to make everything right again. He kept that promise when he sent his Son, Jesus. So whenever you see a rainbow, you can remember: the God who never breaks a promise loves you, and he always will.

reward.name: The Rainbow Feather
reward.text: You uncovered a treasure! Come back tomorrow to keep exploring the trail.
